correctness.rationale: The change of variables gives a monic squarefree degree-eight hyperelliptic model at i=2 modulo 5, so the reduction is good of genus three with two points at infinity. Independent finite-field enumeration gave 7, 43, 133 points and power sums -1, -17, -7, giving the stated numerator by Newton identities and reciprocity. For h(X)=X^3g(X+5/X), g is irreducible by the rational-root test and has discriminant 761. The product of the three quadratic discriminants is -49*71. At an unramified prime over 71, precisely one discriminant has valuation one (g and U^2-20 have only U=34 in common modulo 71); conjugation isolates each of the other discriminants as well. This proves square-class independence and the full wreath group. If a root satisfied alpha^2/5 equal to a root of unity, all its conjugates would have 5-adic valuation 1/2, impossible because the middle coefficient 11 is a unit. The independent pair swaps then exclude root-of-unity quotients between different pairs as well. Powers of the roots thus remain distinct and transitive, giving irreducibility over every finite extension in the sense of the Frobenius polynomial over Q. This excludes a proper abelian subvariety. A complex splitting would give a nontrivial rational endomorphism idempotent defined over a finite number-field extension (endomorphisms are unchanged under algebraically closed base extension); good-reduction specialization injects rational endomorphisms, contradicting geometric simplicity of the reduction. A map to genus one or two would yield a positive-dimensional proper Jacobian quotient by push-pull. The finite checks are arithmetic certificates, not a replacement for the group and specialization arguments.
